title: What does it really mean if we don't practice it?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What have you done lately that matches what you say you stand for?

groups.heading: What does it really mean if we don't practice it?

lines.text: A student said that being exposed to other cultures taught them to appreciate more of what we have, and that they would like to write a book about their life experience. I said: that's a beautiful statement. I think it's courageous to have intent, and consistent intent.

Like I tell my children, I said: if you say you want to be a world champion, it's not that one day you decide, and the next day you forget, and two weeks go by and you weren't consistent with the promise you made to yourself. That's where everything breaks down.

We all love to have intent, I said. But what does it really mean if we don't practice it, if we don't get into the habit, the thought habits, and then make an action? People say, I want to be a really nice guy, and then do something nasty to somebody.

And just because you don't have money doesn't mean you can be unethical, I said. The first thing I say to a company we do business with is: we want to align ourselves with companies that have similar values. It is important to come out and say it.

As I retell it, the author set up a fund for his cause, recruited an expert to run it, along with his son, and so had a team and a structure. He has an idea, he has a mission, he passes it on, and then he creates a structure, a team, and he meets with them, and they have goals. He follows through.

Being outdoors was a chance to unwind, the author says, as I read. What connected with me, I said, is enjoying nature with my children, those significant moments. Those are positive anchors in our life. The more positive anchors you have with your child, the more impact on them as an adult.

At the end I asked the group: if you want to comment on how I explain the chapters, or on the method, or how to improve these calls, I'm totally open. My intent is to extract learning outcomes of what the author was doing, and how it can be significant in our lives.
What is one habit that turns your intent into action?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write an intent you have stated.
Write the habit that would make it real.
Write what you did this week that matches it.
Write the values you want in the companies you work with.
Write the team and structure you will put around your mission.

check.q: What did I say we all love to have?
What did I say is where everything breaks down?
choices: Not being consistent with the promise you made to yourself

check.q: What did I say to align with, in the companies you work with?

recap: Intent needs practice. Build habits, align with your values, and create a structure.
